value.overview: The Cattle Tyrant (Machetornis rixosa) is a distinctive South American tyrant flycatcher that often walks or runs on the ground rather than spending most of its time in trees. It commonly follows cattle, horses, capybaras, and other large animals, capturing insects disturbed by their movement. The species is generally approachable and is associated with open landscapes. In Costa Rica, it is not a regular widespread species but has been documented as an unusual visitor.
value.classification: The Cattle Tyrant belongs to the tyrant flycatcher family, Tyrannidae, in the order Passeriformes. It is the only species in the genus Machetornis.
value.identification: This medium-sized flycatcher is about 19 centimeters long. It has an olive-brown back, grayish head, dark wings and tail, and bright yellow underparts. The bill and legs are black, the legs are relatively long, and the eyes are reddish. A narrow dark line may show through the eye. Males can have a concealed orange crown patch that is raised or exposed during displays. Its habit of walking near grazing animals helps distinguish it from similar kingbirds.
value.rangeHabitat: The main range extends across much of eastern and central South America, from northern Argentina and Bolivia through Brazil, with additional populations in northern South America and parts of Panama and Colombia. It favors open, warm habitats such as cattle pasture, savanna, agricultural land, marsh edges, parks, and lightly wooded areas. In Costa Rica, it appears to be an exceptionally rare or irregular occurrence rather than an established regular species; documented records include observations in Alajuela and Puntarenas, but it is not generally expected on standard Costa Rican bird lists.
value.migrationStatus: Mostly resident within its established range, with local movements rather than long-distance migration. In Costa Rica, records are best treated as rare or irregular occurrences, and there is no reliable evidence of a regular seasonal migration through the country.
value.breeding: The species usually breeds in open country, including pasture, savanna, farmland, and areas near human settlement. It nests in cavities, abandoned nests, or other sheltered sites and may also use structures or nest boxes where available. Both adults defend a territory and care for the young. Breeding information specifically for Costa Rica is not reliably established because the species is not known to form a regular breeding population there.
value.dietFeeding: The Cattle Tyrant feeds mainly on insects and other arthropods captured from the ground or in low vegetation. It often follows cattle, horses, capybaras, and other large animals, taking insects flushed by their movements. It may also seize prey around dung, along muddy margins, or in short grass. Small vertebrates and other food items may occasionally be taken, but invertebrates make up most of its diet.
value.behavior: This active, terrestrial flycatcher frequently walks, runs, or makes short hops across open ground. It commonly perches on fence posts, low branches, livestock, or other elevated points before dropping down to capture prey. Pairs may be territorial and confrontational toward intruders, reflecting the species’ aggressive common-name theme. It is often conspicuous because of its bright yellow underside, upright posture, and tendency to forage in the open.

conservation.populationTrend: The global population is not considered to be undergoing a significant decline. Precise population estimates are unavailable.
